item.content:encoded: Im Streit um schärfere Kapitalvorschriften zeichnet sich für die Schweizer Großbank UBS (UBSG.S) neuer Gegenwind ab. Vertreter der liberalen FDP dürften sich bei der am Donnerstag anstehenden Abstimmung in der kleinen Kammer (Ständerat) dafür aussprechen, auf eine Behandlung des Themas zu verzichten, sagte der Abgeordnete Andrea Caroni am Mittwoch zur Nachrichtenagentur Reuters. Die Mehrheit der FDP-Vertreter im Ständerat werde wohl dafür stimmen, das Vorhaben an die Regierung (Bundesrat) zurückzuweisen. "Ich rechne mit einer Mehrheit meiner Gruppe und bin hoffnungsvoll, dass die Motion angenommen wird", so Caroni. Die Regierung hat in der Sache eine harte Position eingenommen, die die UBS strikt ablehnt. Die Regierung in Bern will mit einem Maßnahmenpaket verhindern, dass es nach dem Zusammenbruch der Credit Suisse im Jahr 2023 und deren anschließender Übernahme durch die UBS zu einer erneuten Banken-Schieflage kommt. Der Vorschlag des Bundesrates würde dem Vermögensverwaltungsriesen zusätzliche Kernkapitalanforderungen von rund 20 Milliarden Dollar aufbürden. Die UBS bekämpft den Vorstoß, weil sie so weniger Geld für Wachstum und Ausschüttungen an die Aktionäre zur Verfügung hätte. Die einflussreiche Kommission für Wirtschaft und Abgaben der kleinen Kammer (Ständerat) überwies Ende August einen wesentlich sanfteren Gegenvorschlag zur Regierungsvorlage. So soll die UBS ihre ausländischen Tochtergesellschaften mit 50 Prozent hartem Kernkapital (CET1) und 50 Prozent sogenannten AT1-Anleihen unterlegen. Die Regierung mit Finanzministerin Karin Keller-Sutter fordert dagegen 100 Prozent hartes Kernkapital, das für die Bank wesentlich teurer ist als AT1-Anleihen. Bisher hatte sich abgezeichnet, dass der Kommissionsvorschlag im Ständerat gute Chancen haben würde. Doch am Dienstag beschlossen FDP-Vertreter, Caronis Vorstoß zu unterstützen. Der Bundesrat sei das richtige Gremium, um über Eigenkapitalanforderungen zu entscheiden, das stehe bereits im Bankengesetz, erklärte Caroni. Die Fraktion der FDP kommt im Ständerat auf zwölf der insgesamt 46 Sitze. Die größte Fraktion ist die Mitte mit 15 Sitzen. Mitte-Vertreter Fabio Regazzi bezweifelte, dass der Antrag Caronis eine Mehrheit finden werde. Regazzi beschrieb die Situation jedoch als "flüssig"; es seien noch verschiedene Ausgänge denkbar.

item.title: After another rally, Guardians eager to pass White Sox atop AL Central
item.description: The Cleveland Guardians recorded their fourth walk-off win this month on Tuesday to remain hot on the heels of the Chicago White Sox in the American League Central.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Cleveland Guardians recorded their fourth walk-off win this month on Tuesday to remain hot on the heels of the Chicago White Sox in the American League Central. Fresh off that late uprising, the Guardians (77-75) can move into sole possession of first place in the division on Wednesday afternoon should they notch a win over the White Sox (77-74) in the decisive matchup of a three-game series in Cleveland. Chicago has held at least a share of first place in the division every day since July 4. Brayan Rocchio's two-run double with two outs in the ninth inning carried Cleveland to a 7-6 victory over Chicago on Tuesday. The walk-off hit was the major-league leading fourth of the season for Rocchio, who is no stranger to coming through in the clutch. After all, he belted a three-run homer in the 10th inning to give the Guardians the AL Central title on the final day of the 2025 regular season. "Unbelievable. I mean, he just has a knack for coming through," Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt said of Rocchio. "He wants to win. He stays calm in those moments. It's such a difficult thing to do, I know, to get a hit. It's so hard to get a hit, and in those moments, he seems to come through. It's a huge, huge moment for us." Rocchio reached base three times on Tuesday and is batting .300 (12-for-40) with three homers and 13 RBIs in his past 12 games. While the Guardians reveled in the victory, White Sox left fielder Sam Antonacci was left to lament coming up short on his lunging attempt to grab Rocchio's game-winning hit. "It's definitely frustrating," a somber Antonacci told reporters after his team's sixth loss in eight games. "They hit the first punch and we punch right back. ... We keep on punching and keep on tacking on runs. We work the whole game to get out to a lead, and to let it go like that, it's frustrating." The White Sox would like to take out their frustrations on Cleveland left-hander Parker Messick (11-9, 2.51 ERA), who will get the start on Wednesday afternoon. Messick allowed one run on three hits in 5 1/3 innings in a no-decision in a 6-2 win against the Minnesota Twins on Friday. He has faced the White Sox on four occasions (all starts) in his young career, including three times this season. All told, he is 2-1 with a 2.10 ERA versus Chicago. The White Sox are expected to hand the ball to left-hander Anthony Kay (9-9, 4.53) on Wednesday. Kay fell to 0-4 in his past six outings after yielding three runs on five hits in four innings during a 7-3 setback to the St. Louis Cardinals on Friday. His most recent win came against Cleveland on Aug. 8, when he allowed two runs on six hits in six innings in a 6-3 victory. Kay is 1-0 with a 1.56 ERA in five career appearances (three starts) versus the Guardians. Cleveland hopes to have rookie Chase DeLauter (right wrist soreness) and Angel Martinez (right side inflammation) back in the lineup for the series finale after both sat out on Tuesday. "We're very day-to-day with both Chase and Angel," Vogt said. --Field Level Media

item.title: Alemania propone medidas de seguridad más estrictas tras el ataque durante el Orgullo en Berlín
item.description: El Gobierno alemán propuso nuevas medidas para prevenir la violencia extremista, entre las que se incluyen penas más severas para los ataques con arma blanca y la propaganda, después de que un hombre que juró lealtad al Estado Islámico atacara una celebración del Orgullo en Berlín este verano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Gobierno alemán propuso nuevas medidas para prevenir la violencia extremista, entre las que se incluyen penas más severas para los ataques con arma blanca y la propaganda, después de que un hombre que juró lealtad al Estado Islámico atacara una celebración del [USN:L6N43R06H TEXT:"Orgullo"] en Berlín este verano. A continuación se detallan las propuestas presentadas el miércoles por el ministro del Interior, Alexander Dobrindt, y la ministra de Justicia, Stefanie Hubig: Se ampliará el uso de tobilleras electrónicas, lo que restringirá la libertad de movimiento de los sospechosos de alto riesgo. Los ataques con arma blanca se tipificarán como delitos graves con una pena mínima de prisión de un año. Se concederá a los 16 gobiernos regionales de Alemania mayor competencia para almacenar datos de comunicaciones como parte de las medidas de seguridad preventivas. Hubig también señaló que las autoridades pretenden aclarar en qué casos son adecuadas las condenas suspendidas. "Si las consecuencias de un posible delito —o incluso de un delito anterior— pudieran ser tremendas para la población, esto debe tenerse en cuenta de forma explícita", dijo. En julio, un hombre de 21 años atacó la celebración del Orgullo de Berlín, matando a una mujer e hiriendo a decenas de personas, según los investigadores. El ciudadano alemán, que en mayo fue declarado culpable y condenado a una pena de prisión por preparar un ataque, había sido puesto en libertad vigilada.

item.title: Mónaco celebrará una de las 10 pruebas de sprint de Fórmula 1 de la temporada 2027, un récord
item.description: Las estrechas y sinuosas calles de Mónaco acogerán por primera vez la próxima temporada una carrera sprint de Fórmula 1, en un calendario récord de 10 fines de semana de carrera —incluida la prueba inaugural prevista en Baréin—, según se dio a conocer este miércoles en un calendario de 24 pruebas.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Las estrechas y sinuosas calles de Mónaco acogerán por primera vez la próxima temporada una carrera sprint de Fórmula 1, en un calendario récord de 10 fines de semana de carrera —incluida la prueba inaugural prevista en Baréin—, según se dio a conocer este miércoles en un calendario de 24 pruebas. El campeonato comenzará en el circuito de Sakhir el 14 de marzo, tras las pruebas que se celebrarán del 24 al 27 de febrero en el reino del golfo Pérsico, y Arabia Saudita acogerá la segunda prueba el 21 de marzo, según anunciaron la F1 y la FIA, organismo rector de este deporte. Portugal (20 de junio) y Turquía (3 de octubre) se incorporan al calendario, mientras que el Gran Premio de Países Bajos en Zandvoort y el de Barcelona fueron eliminados. No figuraban asteriscos junto a las cuatro carreras del golfo, pero su celebración seguirá siendo incierta mientras persista el conflicto actual en la región. La carrera de Arabia Saudita en Yeda se canceló este año, mientras que la de Baréin se ha reprogramado para el circuito de Sepang, en Malasia, el próximo mes. SORPRESA EN MÓNACO La inclusión de una carrera sprint en Mónaco sorprenderá a algunos, dado que adelantar es casi imposible en el trazado junto al puerto del principado. La clasificación suele ser el momento más emocionante del fin de semana de Mónaco, ya que la carrera suele ser una procesión y la gana quien sale desde la pole position. La F1 ha destacado el hecho de que los espectadores podrán disfrutar ahora de dos sesiones de clasificación, además del gran premio estrella del domingo. Sustituir la segunda sesión de entrenamientos del viernes por una clasificación de sprint debería aumentar la emoción en el primer día de acción en pista, pero también dará a los pilotos mucho menos tiempo para adaptarse al fin de semana en un circuito especialmente implacable. Una victoria en la carrera sprint del sábado vale ocho puntos para el ganador, lo que significa que un piloto puede salir del fin de semana con un máximo de 33 puntos, en lugar de los 25 habituales, si gana ambas pruebas. La temporada de 2026 contó con seis sprints, el mayor número hasta la fecha, pero el presidente ejecutivo de la F1, Stefano Domenicali, afirmó en agosto que ese número aumentaría, ya que muchos circuitos querían incluir uno desde que se introdujo el formato en 2021. La F1 señaló que sus datos muestran que la audiencia total de los fines de semana con sprints es un 12% superior a la de los fines de semana que no los tienen, y que la clasificación era tres veces más popular entre los aficionados que los entrenamientos libres. El circuito de Sakhir (Baréin), Australia (Melbourne), Japón (Suzuka), Mónaco y Abu Dabi (Yas Marina) acogerán carreras sprint por primera vez. Las carreras sprint que regresan serán las de Canadá (Montreal), Reino Unido (Silverstone), Italia (Monza), Brasil (Interlagos) y Qatar (Lusail). Esto significa que tres de las cuatro primeras rondas serán carreras sprint, al igual que tres de las cuatro últimas. "Estamos encantados de dar la bienvenida a Portugal y Turquía al campeonato y de ampliar las carreras sprint a diez pruebas, lo que ofrecerá a nuestros aficionados aún más intensidad, emoción y esa acción rueda a rueda que hace que nuestro deporte sea tan especial", afirmó Domenicali. Australia (4 de abril), Japón (11 de abril) y China (18 de abril) formarán un bloque de tres carreras en fines de semana consecutivos, antes de que Miami ocupe su lugar en solitario el 2 de mayo, seguida de Canadá y Mónaco el 23 de mayo y el 6 de junio, respectivamente. Azerbaiyán (26 de septiembre), Turquía (3 de octubre) y Singapur (10 de octubre) forman otra serie de tres carreras consecutivas, mientras que Austin (24 de octubre), México (31 de octubre) y Brasil (7 de noviembre) conforman la tercera. La próxima temporada terminará más tarde que este año, con dos fines de semana de carreras sprint consecutivos en Qatar (5 de diciembre) y Abu Dabi (12 de diciembre). La última carrera de este año está programada para el 6 de diciembre en Abu Dabi, aunque podría reprogramarse para celebrarse esa misma fecha en el circuito italiano de Imola.

item.title: Pelo menos 60 pessoas morrem em desabamento em mina de ouro no Sudão, dizem fontes
item.description: Pelo menos 60 pessoas morreram em um desabamento em uma mina de ouro no Estado de Kordofan Ocidental, no Sudão, no domingo, segundo informaram três fontes à Reuters, enquanto um grupo de direitos humanos local afirmou que alguns mineiros ainda poderiam estar vivos no subsolo e apelou por esforços urgentes de resgate.
item.dc:creator: Khalid Abdelaziz
item.content:encoded: Pelo menos 60 pessoas morreram em um desabamento em uma mina de ouro no Estado de Kordofan Ocidental, no Sudão, no domingo, segundo informaram três fontes à Reuters, enquanto um grupo de direitos humanos local afirmou que alguns mineiros ainda poderiam estar vivos no subsolo e apelou por esforços urgentes de resgate. O grupo de monitoramento Observatório de Kordofan informou nesta quarta-feira que mais de 70 mineiros artesanais estavam mortos ou desaparecidos após o desabamento de uma série de poços de mineração adjacentes na mina de al-Zara, na região de Fouja, a noroeste de al-Nuhud. Citando relatos de testemunhas oculares, o grupo disse que um sobrevivente saiu na terça-feira e relatou que outros ainda estavam vivos no subsolo. O grupo afirmou que nenhuma equipe especializada de resgate estava agindo e que o solo arenoso e instável estava dificultando as tentativas dos moradores de resgatar os mineiros e recuperar os corpos usando ferramentas básicas. As três fontes locais, em declarações à Reuters nesta quarta-feira, atribuíram o elevado número de mortos no local remoto à falta de procedimentos de segurança e de equipamentos de resgate. O Sudão é um dos maiores produtores de ouro da África, mas a grande maioria de seu ouro é extraída por meio de mineração artesanal perigosa e, posteriormente, contrabandeada para fora do país. A mineração de ouro é uma fonte essencial de receita para as Forças de Apoio Rápido, grupo paramilitar que controla o Estado.

item.title: Man City boss Maresca laments VAR row dominating discussion after win
item.description: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca said the debate surrounding the VAR decision that awarded Erling Haaland's winning goal against Manchester United should not overshadow his side's performance in Sunday's 1-0 derby victory with 10 men.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca said the debate surrounding the VAR decision that awarded Erling Haaland's winning goal against Manchester United should not overshadow his side's performance in Sunday's 1-0 derby victory with 10 men. Haaland's second-half strike was initially ruled out for offside before being awarded following a VAR review that judged the Norwegian to be onside. Refereeing body Pro Ref l[USN:L6N45509G TEXT:"ater acknowledged that"] VAR had been wrong to allow the decisive goal. City were reduced to 10 men in the 23rd minute when Phil Foden was sent off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes but held on to secure the win. "To talk about one moment after that game when we played for 70, 75 minutes with 10 players is quite poor. I think the performance was unbelievable and I'm pleased," Maresca told reporters on Wednesday ahead of Thursday's League Cup third-round tie against Norwich City. "There is knowledge that there was a mistake and that's all. Sometimes it goes for you, sometimes against you." The City boss also pointed to a controversial decision in a 2-1 defeat by Manchester United in January 2023, saying the club was still waiting for an apology after Fernandes scored despite Marcus Rashford being in an offside position. Maresca was an assistant coach at City at the time. "Three years ago when I was here, it happened the exact same against Manchester United. The goal was not a regular goal and no one apologised. We are still waiting for the apology for that," he said. Maresca added that VAR officials often had little time to make difficult decisions and mistakes were inevitable. "It's not easy for the VAR and the people in front of the screen. To make a decision in 10, 20 seconds is not easy for them. Sometimes they make mistakes."

item.title: Oxford prof Eccles says AI can help end the ESG wars: Ross Kerber
item.description: The opinions expressed in this column are those of the author, a correspondent for Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Ross Kerber
item.content:encoded: The opinions expressed in this column are those of the author, a correspondent for Reuters. Pollution, public health risks and greenhouse gas emissions are examples of things that economists call "negative externalities," the hidden costs that businesses impose on the rest of us, which do not show up in corporate financial statements. Some executives have tried to bridge the gap with sustainability reports showing data like pollution rates or power consumption. Notably, many companies keep issuing these reports despite the anti-ESG pressure from Republicans in statehouses and in Washington, D.C. But the sustainability reports still largely leave it up to investors to decide how to price environmental impacts. Putting the data to use has been a goal of Robert Eccles, whom I spoke with for this week's column via video from his home near Boston. Eccles is a visiting professor of management at the University of Oxford’s Said Business School who previously taught at Harvard Business School and elsewhere. He's also the co-author, with Columbia's Shivaram Rajgopal, of a new book on how to map financial sustainability details to specific line items in corporate documents like income and cash flow statements and balance sheets. The title, "Making Sustainability Financially Relevant: A Man/Machine Collaboration" nods at how the two used artificial intelligence to zero in on key report details and slash from 100 to 30 the number of hours an expert would need to estimate the financial consequences of the material risks facing a company. (AI advances have probably slashed that number down to around three hours since the book was finished in the spring, Rajgopal told me.) Here's a transcript of our conversation, edited for length and clarity. Q: Bob, you and I have talked a lot about sustainability reporting. Why don't you talk a little about the impetus for this (book) and what you found? A: For a long time, nobody really knew what ESG was. And then they kind of thought it was philanthropy and then sort of didn't like it. And then it's about the material issues, you know, sector specific that matter to value creation. It's funny because the haters of ESG didn't start out with Republicans and we'll get to them in a second. It was people on the left. They were like, “companies should be making the world a better place.” And they didn't like capitalism. Then the right comes along, you know, with Mike Pence and his famous article in the Wall Street Journal . So (with) Shiva, who's a brilliant guy, an accounting professor at Columbia Business School, we had an idea: you take a company's 10-K, you look at risk factors, you look in the footnotes, you identify things that the company has disclosed itself. You compare those to the SASB material issues . Don't take SASB as gospel, but you know, it's a good place to start. Q: One of the things you wrote in the book is that it's really for directors, for example, (to ask themselves): "Who in the organization owns the relationship between sustainability risk and financial exposure? In most companies, the answer is no one." A: Organizational choices vary, but the obvious solution is to have the CSO (chief sustainability officer) report to the CFO (the chief financial officer). The CSO has to be able to understand financial stuff and the CFO needs to understand sustainability stuff. Q: Tell me about Exxon. (XOM.N) Exxon is interesting because they're so big and also because some of their stances are unpredictable until you think about their place in the market. They were backers of the U.S. staying in the Paris Climate Agreement , for example. ON USING AI A: Shiva analyzed ExxonMobil's 10K, and it took him like 100 hours. But he couldn't get to the precision and estimates in terms of what the relative impacts were. He did the analysis, which is a set of prompts. He was using ChatGPT. Then, I developed sort of a so-called black box model. Where it was just like a gigantic prompt, to oversimplify it. With ExxonMobil, we basically took the data in their 10K and we can show that pretty much all of the SASB (Sustainability Accounting Standards Board) issues are addressed. [An Exxon representative declined to comment for this column.] Q: I've had this pet theory that the AI era will be a boom for journalism because at the end of the day, the journalist is assimilating all this information from wherever, but then putting their name on it to say, I am responsible for this content here. And it has seemed to me like in many realms, this is where the opportunity for humans in the AI world is, to check and have the expertise to check what the AI is telling you. Maybe that's not a new insight. A: It's the right insight, and things are going in the other direction....You've got all of these arguments in the academic literature (that users should) disclose AI and how you can only use it together, it's like, no, everybody lies about it anyway. And so what do you care if the human being puts their name on it? Q: This sounds a lot like Bob Dylan ripping off every other folk singer in sight in the '60s at the Café Wha?, to assimilate this new form of music that we all attribute to him. A: But here's the thing, was he really ripping off or was he just building on, like what's original? Everybody's ideas build on previous work, conversations they had with colleagues. Ideas evolve. THE NEBRASKA-DELOITTE FRENEMYSHIP Q: Let's talk about Nebraska (and) the letter that attorneys for a number of Republican-run states wrote to the Big Four accounting firms. One of the leaders of the letter was the Nebraska Attorney General, Mike Hilgers. You found that Nebraska had actually become a major recipient of environmentally focused funding, using the accounting firm Deloitte. Now, technically, this was under the Republican governor of Nebraska. So it's two different officials. A: Let me start out with a shout-out to Nebraska, you know, because the title of my piece is Nebraska is a Climate Champion . Under the (former President Joe) Biden Administration, the EPA selected Nebraska, Nebraska got (an award) for $307 million. On a per capita basis, this is the highest by far. A lot of it went to the Agricultural Data Bank and Grants Program. They've got Deloitte helping them with their climate stuff. They've got Deloitte helping them on the financial side with their internal controls. Q: I think you regard this letter as posturing? Or something else? A: The letter was sent to the Big Four firms, including Deloitte, and it basically accuses them of supporting external standards for climate reporting so that they can make money on it. They ask all these questions, and it's interesting because they express these concerns that they have no data whatsoever that any of these problems that they're concerned about exist, but it's interesting, there's no deadline to respond. So it's kind of like getting this in the public eye, get some attention. It's theater. [A representative for Hilgers declined to comment. Deloitte representatives did not respond to requests for comment] THE FUTURE OF ESG Q: We're in a moment where social and environmental reporting is in retreat. Where are we headed? How well do you think companies have balanced the competing political pressures on them? A: Companies kind of created the opening to be attacked. They confounded value creation with making the world a better place. They would talk in their sustainability reports about the sustainable development goals. That's about making the world a better place. I'm not opposed to that. I don't want to live in a bad world. But you need to distinguish between "these are the material issues that matter to value creation" and "here's how we're managing them, and these other things we really can't deal with because that requires regulation and legislation." So they were sloppy and you had these completely separate, as we talked about earlier, the sustainability function and the financial function. Do I think that the Republican red-state attorneys general and governors are coming from an intellectually sound place? No, I don't. I think they're idiotic in what they're doing. It's been good political theater. Companies left themselves exposed to it. They were playing defense with the left, now they're playing defense with the right. I'm actually quite encouraged because I think this is a good wake-up call for companies. And again, just to pitch my book with Shiva a little bit, the solution is pretty simple. And it's boring. The boring is good. It's like, okay, these are the material issues we think matter for value creation. Here's how we think they affect financial performance, income statement, balance sheet. I think companies need to quit playing defense. They should go on offense. It's not like they need to be, you know, screaming at Trump or Republicans, just like, here's our narrative. These are the sustainability issues we think matter to value creation.

item.title: US court dismisses 4chan's case against Britain's media regulator
item.description: U.S. internet forums 4chan and Kiwi Farms' lawsuit against Britain's media regulator Ofcom has been dismissed by a court in Washington DC, which said it did not have jurisdiction to rule on the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: U.S. internet forums 4chan and Kiwi Farms' [USN:L8N3UK0J1 TEXT:"lawsuit"] against Britain's media regulator Ofcom has been dismissed by a court in Washington DC, which said it did not have jurisdiction to rule on the matter. The owners of the forums clashed with Ofcom over its enforcement of Britain's Online Safety Act, legislation which has caused broader tension between U.S. tech companies and Britain. Critics of the law, which is designed to protect children and vulnerable users from illegal content online, have said it threatens free speech. The British government has "fully backed" Ofcom in taking action. 4chan, an irreverent site that hosts content including pornography and conspiracy theories, and Kiwi Farms had said "threatening communications" they had received from the British regulator interfered with their constitutional rights and operations. Ofcom had accused both of failing to respond to its statutory information requests. Ofcom sent 4chan a "provisional notice of contravention" on August 12, 2025, that threatened to impose a fine of £20,000 ($27,000) as well as daily fines of £100 for up to 60 days. 4chan brought its suit later that month. The regulator imposed the fine — the first under the new regime — in October. The U.S. court ruling, dated Tuesday, said the plaintiffs could defend themselves in British courts. It added that if Ofcom obtained a judgment, that would most likely have to be enforced in the United States, because the companies had no presence or operations abroad. At that point they could take their case to U.S. courts, the judgment said. "Put simply, plaintiffs' suit fails because they seek to use American courts as a sword against Ofcom rather than as a shield to protect themselves," District Judge Rudolph Contreras said. An Ofcom spokesperson said: "A U.S. Court has acknowledged that we are within our rights as a UK regulator to investigate breaches of the UK's online safety laws, and has dismissed claims by 4chan and Kiwi Farms who have sought to stop us doing our job of creating a safer life online for people in the UK." ($1 = 0.7424 pounds)

item.title: Drone shot down in Lithuania was likely aimed at Ukraine, Lithuanian president says
item.description: The drone shot down in Lithuania by an Italian NATO fighter jet on Tuesday was of a type used by Russia and was most likely targeted at Ukraine, Lithuania's president said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Andrius Sytas
item.content:encoded: The drone [USN:L1N4560XG TEXT:"shot down"] in Lithuania by an Italian NATO fighter jet on Tuesday was of a type used by Russia and was most likely targeted at Ukraine, Lithuania's president said on Wednesday. "It was a Gerbera drone," Gitanas Nauseda told reporters on Wednesday, referring to a cheap plywood long-range aerial drone used by Russia. Gerbera drones are often used as decoys but can also carry explosives. "It was most likely not a conscious action against Lithuania. It [the drone] was probably targeted towards Ukraine but affected by Ukrainian electronic warfare and deviated off course," he added. The Lithuanian army is analysing the drone's electronics to determine its targeting, Nauseda said. The drone is the first suspected Russian drone shot down by the NATO Baltic Air Defence mission, which has patrolled the skies in the region since the Baltic states joined NATO in 2004. Countries on NATO's eastern flank have seen repeated drone incursions, fuelling fears of the war between Russia and Ukraine spilling over the alliance's borders. Russia has not commented on the incident. "The security situation has not changed," Nauseda said. Although there is no large-scale operation against Lithuania or NATO, there could still be "certain incidents, provocation, sabotage acts, including false-flag operations," he added. Attacks against Russian opposition activists or Ukrainian supporters are also possible, he said. Polish prosecutors said on Wednesday that a drone spotted in the Baltic sea and later washed up on a [USN:L1N4560AE TEXT:"Polish beach"] on Monday was a Russian Gerbera 2 drone according to preliminary findings. Colonel Bartosz Okoniewski, the deputy district prosecutor for military affairs at the District Prosecutor's Office in Poznan, told state news agency PAP the drone was carrying a warhead which was neutralised on the beach overnight.

item.title: España aumenta la inversión en la red eléctrica a más de 17.000 millones de euros hasta 2030
item.description: El Gobierno español ha decidido aumentar la inversión en la red de transporte eléctrico hasta superar los 17.000 millones de euros (19.600 millones de dólares) de aquí a 2030, lo que supone un 30% más de lo previsto inicialmente, dijo el miércoles la ministra de Energía, Sara Aagesen, alegando el aumento de la demanda derivada de la electrificación.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Gobierno español ha decidido aumentar la inversión en la red de transporte eléctrico hasta superar los 17.000 millones de euros (19.600 millones de dólares) de aquí a 2030, lo que supone un 30% más de lo previsto inicialmente, dijo el miércoles la ministra de Energía, Sara Aagesen, alegando el aumento de la demanda derivada de la electrificación. La rápida expansión de la capacidad de energía renovable en España, así como la nueva demanda procedente de grandes consumidores de energía, como los centros de datos, han incrementado la necesidad de invertir en las redes eléctricas. "Es la mayor inversión en redes eléctricas de la historia de este país", dijo Aagesen. También señaló que un proceso de consulta pública había puesto de manifiesto un aumento significativo de la demanda de conexiones eléctricas por parte de la industria, el sector residencial y los proyectos de energías renovables. La demanda general de electricidad representó el 41% de las propuestas recibidas en la consulta, seguida de los proyectos de generación de energía, con un 40%, y el almacenamiento de energía, con un 19%. La inversión tiene por objeto respaldar los objetivos nacionales de transición energética y cumplir las metas establecidas en el Plan Nacional de Energía y Clima 2023-2030. Aagesen también señaló que España publicará en breve la normativa para crear un mercado de capacidad basado en subastas para el sistema eléctrico, abierto a las empresas de generación y almacenamiento de energía, así como a algunos clientes. En virtud de este mecanismo, los participantes recibirían una compensación por estar disponibles para inyectar electricidad en la red o por reducir el consumo durante los picos de demanda o en situaciones de tensión. (1 dólar = 0,8666 euros)

item.title: German energy firm SEFE boosts gas storage in bid to secure winter reserves
item.description: German state-owned energy firm SEFE said on Wednesday it had independently increased natural gas storage levels as Europe heads into winter with the lowest inventories in years.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Steitz, Holger Hansen
item.content:encoded: German state-owned energy firm SEFE said on Wednesday it had independently increased natural gas storage levels as Europe heads into winter with the lowest inventories in years. Having weaned themselves off cheap and plentiful Russian gas after the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, Germany and other European nations are scrambling to rebuild depleted reserves ahead of the colder months as disruptions to Middle East supplies tighten the global market and push up costs for consumers and industry. A government source told Reuters earlier on Wednesday that economy minister Katherina Reiche would use [USN:L1N45805V TEXT:"market incentives"] to shore up gas storage, while avoiding the direct state purchases that have stoked prices in the past. The government has also agreed with state-owned energy companies Uniper (UN0k.DE) and SEFE that they will make fuller use of their storage capabilities, the source added. SEFE, a gas importer that also operates around a quarter of Germany's gas storage capacity, said it had "taken an independent commercial decision to fill the booked storage capacity". Uniper said that while it was in regular discussions with market participants and authorities, the company alone would decide on how to use its storage assets, adding this would happen "solely on the basis of economic criteria". GAS PRICES HIGHEST SINCE DECEMBER 2022 [USN:L6N4560HI TEXT:"European gas"] prices reached their highest in almost four years this week on faltering diplomatic efforts to open the Strait of Hormuz, through which around a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas supply passed before the Iran war . Germany's gas storage sites were around 53% full in early September, the lowest level for the time of year since records began 15 years ago, according to storage association INES, with the government maintaining that the filling of caverns should be taken care of by the market, not via political intervention. The Economy Ministry said it is ready to take targeted measures for gas supply security if the situation deteriorates. "As a matter of principle, winter preparedness is the responsibility of the market and energy utilities must fulfil their obligations," it said. Uniper said its gas trading business had already stored more gas "than other market players", adding it would meet supply obligations even under challenging market conditions such as a particularly cold winter, and it was suitably prepared.

item.title: In rialzo con futures Usa in attesa Fed, rimbalzo per banche e titoli AI
item.description: Piazza Affari consolida il recupero avviato in apertura, sostenuta dal rimbalzo dei futures Usa, in una mattinata priva di particolari spunti e favorita dal calo dei prezzi del petrolio e dei rendimenti obbligazionari globali.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Piazza Affari consolida il recupero avviato in apertura, sostenuta dal rimbalzo dei futures Usa, in una mattinata priva di particolari spunti e favorita dal calo dei prezzi del petrolio e dei rendimenti obbligazionari globali. L'attenzione del mercato è interamente rivolta alla decisione della Federal Reserve sui tassi attesa in serata. Con un'inflazione ancora sostenuta e il greggio stabilmente sopra i 100 dollari al barile, gli investitori continuano a scontare un rialzo del costo del denaro, il primo dopo il ciclo restrittivo compreso tra marzo 2022 e luglio 2023. "Il focus sarà sulla guidance, o meglio sulla sua assenza, vista la nota ritrosia di Kevin Warsh a fornire indicazioni sulle future mosse di politica monetaria", osservano gli strategist di Mps nella loro nota quotidiana. Intorno alle 12,40 l'indice Ftse Mib (.FTMIB) è in rialzo dello 0,6%. Gli scambi modesti, segnale di una seduta attendista, con 780 milioni di euro in controvalore. Titoli in evidenza: ** Recuperano terreno i bancari dopo due sedute consecutive di vendite, nel giorno dell'atteso rialzo dei tassi Fed. UNICREDIT (CRDI.MI) è la più gettonata con un rialzo dello 0,85% mentre l'istituto ha avviato lunedì il confronto diretto con il governo tedesco in vista dell'aggregazione con Commerzbank, sopratutto sul delicato tema della governance. ** Acquisti, seppur più contenuti, anche sugli altri protagonisti del risiko bancario: INTESA avanza dello 0,5% circa, come BANCO BPM (BAMI.MI) , e MPS (BMPS.MI) dello 0,2%. ** In recupero anche i titoli tech legati all'IA dopo il pesante 'sell-off' delle ultime sedute: PRYSMIAN (PRY.MI) è in cima al FTSE Mib con un progresso del 2,7%, in compagnia di STM che avanza del 2,6%. ** A sostenere l'indice delle blue chip sono anche gli energetici da TENARIS (TENR.MI) e SAIPEM (SPMI.MI) , alle utility A2A (A2.MI) , ITALGAS (IG.MI) e ENEL (ENEI.MI) . ** CAMPARI (CPRI.MI) perde slancio dopo una partenza più brillante e cede lo 0,6% nonostante la promozione di Deutsche Bank a 'buy' da 'hold'. ** In fondo al listino principale STELLANTIS (STLAM.MI) cede il 2,3% dopo che Berenberg ha tagliato il giudizio a 'hold' da 'buy', riducendo il prezzo obiettivo a 5,10 euro da 7,80.

item.title: POINT MARCHÉS Les Bourses progressent à mi-séance, la Fed attendue au tournant
item.description: Wall Street est attendue en hausse et les Bourses européennes progressent mercredi à mi-séance, dans un contexte attentiste avant la décision de la Réserve fédérale (Fed) sur les taux, tandis qu'une légère baisse des cours du pétrole apporte un peu de répit face aux vives craintes d'inflation.
item.dc:creator: Diana Mandia
item.content:encoded: Wall Street est attendue en hausse et les Bourses européennes progressent mercredi à mi-séance, dans un contexte attentiste avant la décision de la Réserve fédérale (Fed) sur les taux, tandis qu'une légère baisse des cours du pétrole apporte un peu de répit face aux vives craintes d'inflation. Les futures sur indices new-yorkais signalent une ouverture en hausse de 0,16% pour le Dow Jones (.DJI) , de 0,22% pour le Standard & Poor's-500 (.SPX) et de 0,44% pour le Nasdaq. À Paris, le CAC 40 (.FCHI) gagne 0,45% à 8.126,38 points vers 10h53 GMT. À Francfort, le Dax (.GDAXI) prend 0,26% et à Londres, le FTSE 100 (.FTSE) gagne de 0,59%. L'indice EuroStoxx 50 (.STOXX50E) avance de 0,46%, le FTSEurofirst 300 (.FTEU3) de 0,53% et le Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) de 0,51%. La banque centrale américaine devrait annoncer ce mercredi une hausse de 25 points de base de son taux d'intérêt, la première depuis 2023, après que l'inflation persistante et un marché du travail suffisamment solide ont conduit les acteurs du marché à revoir rapidement leurs prévisions en l'espace de quelques jours. Selon l'outil FedWatch du CME Group, les marchés estiment à 92,5% la probabilité d'une hausse, contre 61,2% il y a seulement une semaine. Le président de la Fed, Kevin Warsh, irait ainsi à l'encontre du souhait maintes fois exprimé par le locataire de la Maison blanche, Donald Trump, de voir les taux reculer, à un moment où les marchés sont particulièrement soucieux de s'assurer de l'indépendance de la banque centrale vis-à-vis du pouvoir politique. "Pour lui, relever les taux dès maintenant est une question de crédibilité. S'il ne le fait pas ce soir, cela pourrait nuire à la crédibilité de la Fed, à son indépendance et au marché boursier", avertit Michaël Nizard, responsable des stratégiste chez Edmond de Rothschild Asset Management à Paris. La politique monétaire est le sujet phare de la semaine sur les marchés, car, outre la Fed, des décisions sont également attendues de la part de la Banque d'Angleterre (BoE), jeudi, et de la Banque du Japon (BoJ), vendredi, alors que les responsables des banques centrales adoptent une attitude plus ferme face à l'inflation provoqué par le conflit au Moyen-Orient. Au Royaume-Uni, [USN:L8N4580HO TEXT:"les prix"] ont accéléré sur un an en août pour atteindre leur plus haut niveau sur les cinq derniers mois, à 3,1%, mais ces chiffres ne devraient pas trop influencer les prévisions selon lesquelles la BoE maintiendra ses taux inchangés ce mois-ci, avant de les relever à deux reprises d'ici la fin de l'année. Les cours du pétrole offrent en outre un léger répit mercredi, les informations selon lesquelles l'Arabie saoudite proposait des cargaisons supplémentaires de brut via Oman et l'augmentation surprise des stocks aux États-Unis ayant quelque peu apaisé les craintes concernant l'ampleur des perturbations de l'approvisionnement au Moyen-Orient. LES VALEURS À SUIVRE À WALL STREET [USN:L8N4580C8] VALEURS EN EUROPE A Paris, le fabricant français de matériaux pour semi-conducteurs Soitec (SOIT.PA) grimpe de plus de 12% après que JP Morgan a relevé sa recommandation sur la valeur, estimant que les perspectives de son activité de photonique sur silicium l'emportent désormais sur les inquiétudes persistantes liées à la faiblesse des marchés de la téléphonie mobile. Vallourec (VLLP.PA) , qui a annoncé un contrat auprès de l'entreprise parapétrolière Subsea7, gagne 5,6%. L'automobile (.SXAP) est à la traîne par rapport aux autres secteurs du Stoxx (-1,07%), Renault (RENA.PA) reculant de 4,2% et Stellantis (STLAM.MI) de 2,3%. TAUX Les rendements obligataires se stabilisent mercredi à des niveaux proches de leurs pics de près de deux décennies, dans un contexte marqué par les anticipations d'une politique monétaire plus restrictive de la part des banques centrales et par les inquiétudes liées à la dette publique. Aux Etats-Unis, en attendant la Fed, le rendement des Treasuries à dix ans est quasi inchangé à 4,9897% après avoir franchi lundi le seuil des 5% et atteint mardi un plus haut depuis mi-2007. Le rendement du titre à deux ans recule légèrement à 4,6549%. Dans la zone euro, le rendement du Bund allemand à dix ans s'affiche en petite baisse à 3,5339% après avoir connu la veille un plus haut depuis juin 2009. Le deux ans est stable à 3,2360%. En France, le rendement de l'OAT à dix ans s'établit à 4,4970%, proche d'un pic de 18 ans. La croissance des salaires dans la zone euro a par ailleurs continué de ralentir au cours du dernier trimestre, alors même que l'inflation s'accélérait, et les accords salariaux négociés ne laissent entrevoir qu'une légère reprise l'année prochaine, ce qui pourrait rassurer les responsables de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE). Francfort a relevé ses taux d'intérêt la semaine dernière, pour la deuxième fois depuis le début de la guerre au Moyen-Orient. CHANGES Sur le marché des changes, et attendant également la Fed, le dollar évolue sur de faibles variations (+0,08%) face à un panier de devises de référence (.DXY) . L'euro perd 0,08% à 1,1534 dollar . PÉTROLE Le Brent recule de 1,02% à 107,64 dollars le baril et le brut léger américain (West Texas Intermediate, WTI) 1,97% à 103,74 dollars.
